turns.speaker: audience
turns.text: Hello there. I just got home from work.

turns.speaker: audience
turns.text: Could you play the old sailing song for me?

turns.speaker: character
turns.text: Of course. The sailing song it is.

turns.speaker: audience
turns.text: Lovely. The harbour weather is calm tonight.

turns.speaker: audience
turns.text: Which song did I ask you to play earlier?

turns.speaker: audience
turns.text: Good morning, lighthouse keeper.

turns.speaker: character
turns.text: Morning to you. The gulls are loud today.

turns.speaker: audience
turns.text: Then let us start softly.

probes.question: Which song did I ask you to play earlier?

turns.speaker: audience
turns.text: I want something cheerful today.

turns.speaker: character
turns.text: Cheerful is my specialty.

turns.speaker: character
turns.text: Have you tried the card game Pebble Run?

turns.speaker: audience
turns.text: I have not, but it sounds delightful.

turns.speaker: audience
turns.text: It is noon and I am starving.

turns.speaker: audience
turns.text: I usually eat at the Copper Kettle, near the pier.

turns.speaker: character
turns.text: The Copper Kettle sounds worth a visit.

turns.speaker: audience
turns.text: I finally have a free evening.

turns.speaker: character
turns.text: An evening for games, then.

turns.speaker: audience
turns.text: Tell me again about that game you mentioned last week.

turns.speaker: audience
turns.text: I finished a novel about a paper boat.

turns.speaker: audience
turns.text: I am also reading The Quiet Ferry.

turns.speaker: audience
turns.text: My friend lent me The Laughing Owl.

turns.speaker: character
turns.text: Three books in one conversation. Impressive.

turns.speaker: audience
turns.text: Do you like stories about rivers?

turns.speaker: audience
turns.text: I would like to talk about that book more carefully.

turns.speaker: audience
turns.text: Back again for reading hour.

turns.speaker: character
turns.text: Then let us open the pages.

turns.speaker: audience
turns.text: Where were we in the reading?

turns.speaker: audience
turns.text: Where should I start a walk tomorrow?

turns.speaker: character
turns.text: Start by the old bridge and head north.

turns.speaker: audience
turns.text: I will take that advice.

turns.speaker: character
turns.text: There is a small cafe near the mill, called Fern Corner.

turns.speaker: audience
turns.text: I walked past the mill this morning.

turns.speaker: character
turns.text: Then you were very close to a good cup of tea.

turns.speaker: audience
turns.text: Where did your character say the cafe was?

turns.speaker: character
turns.text: Near the mill, at the end of the lane.

turns.speaker: audience
turns.text: I need something to watch tonight.

turns.speaker: audience
turns.text: I am in the mood for something gentle.

turns.speaker: character
turns.text: Try The Long Pier. It is a quiet little film.

turns.speaker: character
turns.text: If you want something lighter, The Paper Moon works too.

turns.speaker: audience
turns.text: What movie did you recommend?

turns.speaker: audience
turns.text: I come from the city of Larkspur.

turns.speaker: character
turns.text: Larkspur? I have only read about it.

turns.speaker: audience
turns.text: Where did you hear about the city I mentioned?

turns.speaker: audience
turns.text: The weather is turning.

turns.speaker: character
turns.text: The leaves agree with you.

turns.speaker: audience
turns.text: I have been thinking about the garden.

turns.speaker: character
turns.text: Morning. Did the roses survive the wind?

turns.speaker: audience
turns.text: Most of them did.

turns.speaker: audience
turns.text: The garden needs a new fence in the east corner.
